iosTitle: Add OmniQR to your Home Screen
iosHelp: In Safari, tap Share, then choose Add to Home Screen.
howIntro: Prepare a QR code in seconds and keep control of your settings.
stepOneText: Pick what you want to share, from a link to a Wi-Fi network.
stepTwoText: Choose colors, module shape, and error correction level.
stepThreeText: Export PNG, vector SVG, JPEG, WebP, or print-ready PDF.
faq1Q: Is my content stored on a server?
faq1A: No. It is sent to the same-origin server to render the QR image and may remain briefly in process memory; it is not persistently stored, tied to an account, or sent to analytics.
faq2Q: How can I make my QR code easier to scan?
faq2A: Use dark modules on a light background, preserve the quiet zone, and avoid overly long content. The readability note gives tips based on contrast and density.
faq3Q: Can I generate a QR code without internet?
faq3A: The cached page can open offline, but generating a new QR image currently requires an internet connection.
faq4A: PNG, true vector SVG, JPEG, WebP, and PDF. Raster exports support resolutions from 512 to 4096 pixels.
faq5Q: Can I add a logo in the center?
faq5A: Center logo embedding is not available yet. High error correction is the foundation for adding a logo in a future version.
faq6Q: How do I install it on my phone?
faq6A: Chrome on Android and desktop shows an install button. On iPhone, open Safari’s Share menu and choose Add to Home Screen.
faq7Q: Which settings should I use for print?
faq7A: Keep at least four modules of quiet zone, use high-contrast colors, and test a printed sample with a real phone.
